subject: Hosted API commit settlement — quarterly remediation schedule (Verdant Retail)
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@verdantretail.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@verdantretail.com>, procurement@verdantretail.com
Date: Tue, 6 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify commit settlement mechanics and make-goods for Q4 overage

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking the time on our last call. We pulled our usage reports and it looks like Verdant exceeded the Q4 hosted API commit by ~18%. Procurement wants to understand:

- How Redwood handles quarterly true-ups versus annual true-ups (timing and mechanics)
- Whether make-goods (credits to cover shortfalls) are issued as invoice offsets or as account credits that roll forward
- Any proration rules if we change commit tiers mid-quarter

Can you share the proposed timeline for remediation (how quickly credits would be applied) and whether we need to sign an amendment for the credit? Attaching our internal usage snapshot if helpful.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Lee
Head of Cloud Ops, Verdant Retail
jordan.lee@verdantretail.com

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@verdantretail.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 7 Jan 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify commit settlement mechanics and make-goods for Q4 overage

Jordan —

Appreciate the note and the usage snapshot. High level answer up front: we do quarterly reconciliations by default for hosted API commits and we offer a one-time make-good to bring usage back in line with the committed volume for the quarter. Details below and attached is a short summary PDF (VerdantCommitSummary_Q1.pdf) that maps your numbers to our billing model.

Quick bullets:
- Quarterly vs annual: QBR reconciliation occurs each quarter; if you prefer an annual true-up we can accommodate that as a contract amendment, but quarterly is standard for hosted usage.
- Make-goods: we issue account credits that can be applied to the next invoice as an offset by default. If you prefer a direct refund we can discuss but credits are typical.
- Timing: once reconciled, credits are applied within 30 calendar days, pending normal approvals (finance/legal).
- Proration: if you increase/decrease commit mid-quarter, we prorate on a per-day basis for the remaining days in the quarter; reductions below 80% utilization can trigger a different treatment — see attached for examples.
- Rollover: we support a limited rollover of unused commit between adjacent quarters (policy configurable in the SOW).

Action items: can you confirm whether Verdant prefers credits applied as invoice offsets or as account credits that roll forward? Also confirm whether you want quarterly reconciliation (default) or annual. If quarterly, I’ll route the make-good flow to finance and attach an amendment template for signatures.

I’ve cc’ed Rishi and Karthik to loop in billing/legal and Tessa for operations intake.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: VerdantCommitSummary_Q1.pdf (summary of Q4 usage and proposed make-good)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@verdantretail.com>

Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:19:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify commit settlement mechanics and make-goods for Q4 overage

Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick summary. A couple of clarifications from Procurement:

1) We prefer credits that roll forward to give us flexibility across seasonal spikes. Is there a cap on how much can roll between quarters?
2) We have a separate Dedicated pool for certain workloads — can credits from hosted API usage be applied to Dedicated invoices, or are they strictly for hosted?
3) We noticed an overage invoice (INV-98122) that was issued in late Dec; do your offsets apply retroactively or only forward from the reconciliation date?

If rolling credits are acceptable and can be applied to hosted only, we can accept that. If they can be applied to Dedicated too, that would be preferable. Happy to take a short call to lock this down.

—Jordan

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@verdantretail.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify commit settlement mechanics and make-goods for Q4 overage

Jordan — quick follow from billing/legal perspective:

- Rollover cap: standard is up to 10% of the committed volume can roll forward to the next adjacent quarter; larger rollovers require an amendment.
- Applicability: Credits created from hosted API reconciliations are scoped to the billing entity that owns the commit. If Verdant’s Dedicated pool is on the same billing entity/account, credits can be used across hosted and dedicated invoices. If Dedicated is billed under a separate contract entity, credits cannot cross-contract without an SOW amendment.
- Retroactive offsets: we can apply offsets to an open overage invoice (INV-98122) if the reconciliation documents the usage shortfall and both sides sign the reconciliation statement. The operational flow typically takes 2–3 billing cycles to fully reconcile internal approvals, but we aim to apply adjustments within 30–45 days.

I’ve attached an internal SOW amendment template and a short checklist for the reconciliation packet (SOW_Verdant_Amendment_v1.docx referenced). If Verdant confirms the rolling-credit preference and confirms the billing entity alignment, we’ll produce an amendment that lists the rollover cap and the make-good timing.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@verdantretail.com>, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, tessa.morgan@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 15:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify commit settlement mechanics and make-goods for Q4 overage

Jordan/Team —

Proposing the following settlement approach to keep things practical and minimize invoicing churn:

1) Quarterly reconciliation (default): compare committed tokens vs actual tokens per quarter.
2) Make-good: issue account credits equal to the shortfall up to the committed amount for that quarter. Credits applied as invoice offsets by default, but can roll forward if requested (subject to rollover cap).
3) Rollover policy: up to 10% of unused commit can roll into the immediately following quarter. Any unused beyond that is forfeited unless an amendment is signed.
4) Retroactive invoice handling: we will issue a reconciliation statement within 14 days of receiving Verdant’s usage confirmation. Upon mutual sign-off, finance will apply credit to open invoices (INV-98122) or issue an offset on the next invoice within 30–45 days.
5) Edge cases: if Verdant decreases commit mid-quarter, credits are prorated daily and make-goods are computed on the final settled commit for the quarter.

Next steps: if Verdant agrees to the above, Redwood will prepare an amendment reflecting the rollover cap and the 30–45 day credit window. Vanessa — can you confirm internal approval and we’ll send the amendment for signature?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Account Strategy, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: SOW_Verdant_Amendment_v1.docx (amendment template)

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@verdantretail.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify commit settlement mechanics and make-goods for Q4 overage

Thanks — Verdant is comfortable with the proposed approach pending one change: instead of forfeiting unused beyond 10%, we’d like a one-time option to rollover up to an additional 10% for the following quarter (so a total possible rollover of 20%) in case of seasonality-driven spikes. If that’s acceptable, Procurement will sign the amendment and we can apply credits to INV-98122 once the reconciliation statement is signed.

If you can add a short clause to the amendment describing the one-time rollover option (and any limits), we’ll move quickly.

Appreciate the responsiveness —
Jordan
